The as -cast ZK60 alloy had a typical dendritic structure which was composed of α magnesium matrix, the eutectic phase and second phase particles. The average grain size of the original as-cast ZK60 alloy was ~150μm.
After solution heat treatment at 430 ˚C for 16 h, most of the eutectic and second phase particles were dissolved in the matrix, and the grain size grew to ~200μm.

attributes.size: fine grains ~2 μm; coarse grains ~10 μm

After the first 4 passes of ECAP , it presented a bimodal structure elongated along the shear direction with both coarse and fine grains. The average size of the fine grains was ~5μm.

attributes.size: ~2 μm average grain size; few coarse grains ~20 μm

evidence.quote: With the number of ECAP passes increased to 6, the coarse grains were refined and the average grain size was continuously refined to ~2μm in diameter. Only a few of the coarse grains were left with size of ~20μm.
It can be seen clearly that LT ECAP 8 pas ses sample possessed super-fine grains with the average grain size only ~500nm

high strength and good ductility were achieved in ZK60 magnesium alloy by a combination of grain refinem ent strengthening and precipitate hardening through the use of heat treatment and equal channel angular pressing (ECAP)

When the processing temperature was gradually reduced, the finer grain size and the increased metastable phase particles supplied synergic fine grain and precipitate hardening, which certainly rendered higher strength of the LT ECAP 8 passes sample.

Some of the precipitates resided along the grain boundaries , which indicated that these precipitates were effective in pinning the grain boundaries and suppressing the dynamic grain recovery or growth.

for the pre -solution heat treated sample, due to the absence of hard particles in the homogenized alloy, the distribution of dislocations and strain were more homogeneous which induced continuous dynamic recry stallization and a more homogeneous microstructure.
Such fine metastable phase particles effectively pinned down the basal dislocations, and non-basal cross slips could be seen activated by the fine particles in Fig. 7 (a).
